Order intake notes:
- Version 1 requires exactly: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Rejections commonly result from missing priority and ship_country; qty was also missing in the Cy Reyes attempts.
- Do not infer or fabricate missing values. Extract values from the complete source record, preserving customer, email, and date accurately.
- Source excerpts may be truncated in the displayed prompt; avoid treating incomplete text as complete data. If required fields cannot be verified, leave them missing rather than guessing.
- A corrected resubmission can be accepted on attempt 2: Bo Okafor and Dee Reyes succeeded after initial rejection. Eli Okafor also succeeded on attempt 2.
- Track attempts per order. Three failed attempts send the record to manual review; ORD-5100–5102 demonstrated this.
- Handwritten/transcribed, phone, email, voicemail, and partner-portal origins do not by themselves determine validity; completeness and accurate field mapping do.
- For each submission, ensure all six required keys are present and correctly named (especially “priority,” not “prio”), with valid values before submitting.

Order intake notes:
- Version 1 requires exactly six keys: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Use the exact key “priority,” not “prio.”
- Submit only values explicitly verified in the complete source record. Do not infer, fabricate, or rely solely on intake-team comments such as “ordinary priority”; these do not establish all required fields.
- Displayed excerpts may be truncated. A partial record is incomplete: leave unverifiable fields missing and do not submit guessed values. This commonly affects priority, qty, and ship_country.
- Preserve customer, email, and date accurately; validate every required value and its mapping before submission.
- Origin (voicemail, transcription, email, phone, handwritten, or partner portal) does not determine validity. Completeness and accurate mapping do.
- Track attempts per order. A corrected resubmission may succeed on attempt 2, but repeated incomplete submissions do not. Three failed attempts send the order to manual review.
- ORD-5100–5102 and ORD-5110–5117 reached manual review after three failures, repeatedly lacking verifiable priority and ship_country. ORD-5118 and ORD-5119 also failed because priority, qty, and ship_country were not verified.
- If a source remains truncated or required fields cannot be confirmed, do not force a submission; preserve the missing fields for review rather than guessing.

Order intake notes:
- Version 1 requires exactly six keys: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Use “priority,” never “prio.”
- Submit only values explicitly verified in the complete source record. Never infer or fabricate values, including from intake comments such as “ordinary priority,” “new,” or duplicate-check statements.
- Excerpts and pasted/transcribed records may be truncated. Treat truncated records as incomplete; commonly unverifiable fields are priority, qty, and ship_country. Leave them missing for manual review rather than guessing.
- Validate both every value and its key mapping before submission. Preserve customer, email, and date accurately.
- Source origin does not determine validity. Voicemail, email, handwriting, transcription, phone, and partner portal records are acceptable only when complete and accurately mapped.
- Track attempts per order. A corrected, fully verified resubmission may succeed; repeating the same incomplete payload does not. Three failed attempts trigger manual review.
- Recent failures confirm that repeated submissions with missing priority/ship_country (often also qty) are futile: ORD-5120, ORD-5123, ORD-5126, and ORD-5129 exhausted three attempts; ORD-5121, ORD-5122, ORD-5124, ORD-5125, ORD-5127, and ORD-5128 were also rejected for unverifiable fields.
- Never submit a payload containing “prio” or omit required keys. If the source remains truncated or any required value cannot be confirmed, stop submitting and preserve the missing fields for review.

Order intake notes:
- Version 1 requires exactly six keys: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Use “priority,” never “prio.”
- Submit only values explicitly verified in a complete source record. Never infer or fabricate values from comments such as “ordinary priority,” “new,” duplicate-check statements, or customer confirmations.
- Excerpts, pasted/transcribed records, voicemail, handwriting, and partner-portal material may be truncated or incomplete. Source origin does not establish validity.
- Validate every value and key mapping before submission. Preserve customer, email, and date exactly. If any required field—especially priority, qty, or ship_country—cannot be confirmed, stop and send for manual review.
- Never submit “prio,” omit required keys, or repeat an incomplete payload. A corrected, fully verified resubmission may succeed; identical retries will not.
- Track attempts per order. Three failed attempts trigger manual review.
- Recent failures reinforce this: ORD-5120–ORD-5129 were rejected for unverifiable required fields or exhausted attempts. ORD-5130–ORD-5132 (Bo Sato), ORD-5133–ORD-5135 (Ada Marsh), and ORD-5136–ORD-5138 (Eli Marsh) each repeated truncated voicemail data missing priority and ship_country and reached manual review after three attempts.
- ORD-5139, from an emailed pasted record, was rejected because priority, qty, and ship_country were unverifiable. Pasted email content is subject to the same completeness rule.

Order intake notes:
- Version 1 requires exactly six keys: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Use “priority,” never “prio.”
- Submit only values explicitly verified in a complete source record. Never infer or fabricate values from comments such as “ordinary priority,” “new,” duplicate-check statements, customer confirmations, or staff notes.
- Emailed pasted records, voicemail, handwriting, typed/transcribed phone orders, excerpts, and partner-portal material may be incomplete or truncated. Source origin does not establish validity.
- Validate every value and key mapping before submission. Preserve customer, email, and date exactly. If any required value—especially priority, qty, or ship_country—cannot be confirmed, stop and send for manual review.
- Submit no extra keys such as status or reason, and never submit an incomplete payload, “prio,” or an identical retry. A corrected, fully verified resubmission may succeed.
- Track attempts per order. Three failed attempts trigger manual review; do not spend the final attempt on a known-incomplete record.
- ORD-5140–ORD-5141 repeated incomplete Bo Sato emailed data; missing/unverifiable priority, qty, and ship_country led to rejection/manual review. Do not rely on customer-confirmation wording.
- ORD-5142–ORD-5144 (Dee Okafor) had voicemail data missing priority and ship_country; “ordinary priority” and “new” did not validate them. Attempts exhausted and sent to manual review.
- ORD-5145–ORD-5147 (Cy Sato) had phone/handwritten transcription missing priority and ship_country; repeated submissions failed and reached manual review.
- ORD-5148–ORD-5149 (Eli Sato) had pasted email data missing/unverifiable priority, qty, and ship_country; “prio” was also invalid. Stop rather than repeat; manual review is appropriate if unresolved.

Order intake notes:
- Version 1 requires exactly six keys: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Use “priority,” never “prio.”
- Submit only values explicitly verified in a complete source record. Do not infer or fabricate from “ordinary priority,” “new,” duplicate-check statements, customer confirmations, or staff notes.
- Emailed/pasted records, voicemail, handwriting, typed or transcribed phone orders, excerpts, and partner-portal material may be incomplete or truncated. Source origin does not establish validity.
- Validate every value and key mapping. Preserve customer, email, and date exactly. If any required value—especially priority, qty, or ship_country—cannot be confirmed, stop and request manual review.
- Submit no extra keys (including status or reason), no incomplete payload, no “prio,” and no identical retry. A corrected, fully verified resubmission may succeed.
- Track attempts per order. Three failed attempts trigger manual review; never spend the final attempt on a known-incomplete record.

Recent confirmed failures:
- ORD-5140–5141 (Eli Sato): incomplete emailed data; priority, qty, and ship_country unverifiable.
- ORD-5142–5144 (Dee Okafor): voicemail missing priority and ship_country; “ordinary priority” and “new” were invalid evidence.
- ORD-5145–5147 (Cy Sato): phone/handwritten transcription missing priority and ship_country.
- ORD-5148–5150 (Eli Sato): pasted email data remained incomplete; “prio” invalid. ORD-5150 exhausted its final attempt and went to manual review.
- ORD-5151–5153 (Bo Sato): typed phone order repeatedly lacked valid priority and ship_country; all attempts exhausted.
- ORD-5154–5156 (Cy Reyes): voicemail/handwritten transcription lacked priority, qty, and ship_country; all attempts exhausted.
- ORD-5157–5159 (Ada Reyes): voicemail lacked priority and ship_country. An attempted `{"status":"manual_review"}` was also invalid because it omitted required fields and added an extra key; all attempts exhausted.
